1930年代各项世界规划参与者之重叠。星号标示日内瓦高等国际问题研究院的教员。

zh: 在这些以国际网络联结的自由主义经济专家群体与李普曼座谈会之间存在重要重叠。例如，康德利夫就出席了1938年的巴黎聚会。哈根·舒尔茨-福贝格（Hagen Schulz-Forberg）提醒人们注意这一背景的重要性，指出米塞斯曾为1936年的ISC贡献了一项关于原材料的研究，迈克尔·海尔佩林则为1937年和1939年的会议撰写并传阅了论文。
米塞斯曾作为高等国际问题研究院的代表出席1936年5月在马德里举行的ISC会议。
勒普克1936年曾设法参加ISC会议，但因持德国护照未能成行。
李普曼其人同样举足轻重。ISC的美方协调机构是外交关系委员会（Council on Foreign Relations）；1937年巴黎会议的（同样由洛克菲勒资助的）美方名单上，李普曼与后来的国务卿约翰·福斯特·杜勒斯、国际法专家菲利普·C.·杰塞普并列。
从这个意义上说，沃尔特·李普曼座谈会不是一次反常的聚会，而是十足的时代产物，是国际商会、国际联盟与美国慈善基金会资助的国际自由主义协作研究之精神的延续。
en: There were important overlaps between these internationally networked groups of liberal economic experts and the CWL. Condliffe, for example, was in attendance in Paris in 1938. Hagen Schulz-Forberg has drawn attention to the importance of this context, pointing out that Mises contributed a study on raw materials to the 1936 ISC and Michael Heilperin wrote and circulated pieces for the 1937 and 1939 meetings.
Mises attended the May 1936 ISC meeting in Madrid as a representative of the Graduate Institute.
Röpke had tried to attend the ISC conference in 1936 but could not because of his German passport.

Also significant was the figure of Lippmann himself. The American coordinating committee for the ISC was the Council on Foreign Relations, and the group (also Rockefeller-funded) for the 1937 conference held in Paris listed Lippmann along with future secretary of state John Foster Dulles and international law expert Philip C. Jessup.

The Walter Lippmann Colloquium, in this sense, was not an anomalous gathering but very much of the time, a continuation of a spirit of international liberal collaborative research funded by the ICC, the League of Nations, and U.S. philanthropic foundations.

zh: 李普曼座谈会持续四天，最后决定在巴黎成立一个自由主义革新国际研究中心，另设瑞士、英国和美国支部，分别由勒普克、哈耶克和李普曼主持。
在法国实业家路易·马利奥——1920年代铝业卡特尔的主要缔造者——的建议下，聚会思想家们为他们的共同意识形态选定的标签是“新自由主义”。
这一新运动的法国中心设在社会博物馆（Musée Social）——这座建筑最初是为保存1889年巴黎博览会社会经济展区文件而建。它被称为“现代法国的社会实验室”，作为刚刚诞生的新自由主义运动的总部似乎不同寻常。
然而，正如学者们所指出的，座谈会上的讨论与市场原教旨主义的刻板形象相去甚远。
与会者立场不一，其中许多主张都倾向于容纳某种形式的干预与福利国家。
en: The Walter Lippmann Colloquium lasted four days and concluded with the decision to create an International Study Center for the Renovation of Liberalism in Paris with Swiss, English, and American outposts overseen by Röpke, Hayek, and Lippmann, respectively.

On the suggestion of the French industrialist Louis Marlio, a major player in the creation of an aluminum cartel in the 1920s, the label on which the gathered thinkers settled for their shared ideology was “neoliberalism.”

The French center for the new movement was to be housed in the Musée Social, a building originally created to hold the documents from the Social Economy exhibition of the 1889 Paris Exhibition. Called a “social laboratory for modern France,” the building may seem like an unlikely headquarters for the just-born neoliberal movement.
Yet, as scholars have noted, the discussions at the CWL hardly conformed to a caricature of market fundamentalism.
Instead participants took a range of positions, many of which clustered around accommodation for some form of intervention and a welfare state.

zh: 李普曼的文本本身为这类借用敞开了大门。这位美国记者对他所称“自由放任的谬误”尖刻辛辣——古典自由主义者由此沦为对现状毫无感召力的辩护人。
在这个问题上，他体现了战间期的时代精神。1924年，凯恩斯已石破天惊地宣告“自由放任的终结”，并建议重新思考保障市场所必需的国家角色。
在李普曼看来，19世纪的自由主义者否认保存市场条件需要强有力的国家——尤其需要法律框架，实际上就等于认可了碰巧占上风的任何状况。李普曼呼吁“自由主义的革新”，后来成立的研究中心沿用了这个提法。这样的革新不仅承认维护市场需要制度，而且认可一整套惊人宽泛、会被认作福利国家的政策选项：从优生学、教育到公共工程与城市游乐设施。
这些服务将通过向富人征税来支付，从中刮取他所谓的“过剩资本”。
en: Lippmann’s text left itself open to such appropriation. The American journalist was scathing about what he called the “fallacy of laissez faire,” by which classical liberals ended up as uninspiring apologists for the status quo.
In this, he reflected the interwar zeitgeist. In 1924 Keynes had already famously declared “the end of laissez faire” and suggested a rethinking of the state necessary to safeguard the market.

In Lippmann’s view, by disavowing the need for a strong state, and especially a legal framework, to preserve the conditions of the market, nineteenth-century liberals had effectively approved of whatever conditions happened to prevail. In the phrase that was attached to the center established in his wake, Lippmann called for a “renovation of liberalism” that not only acknowledged the necessity of institutions in preserving the market but also sanctioned a startlingly broad palette of measures one would identify with the welfare state: from eugenics and education to public works and urban recreation facilities.
These services would be paid for through taxes on the wealthy, skimming off what he called “excess capital.”

zh: 李普曼其书以及围绕它组织的座谈会，最引人注目的特征是：像勒普克和哈耶克这样对这类干预与再分配形式素来怀疑的思想家，竟会对此如此热情。不妨猜测：这本书最令人解脱之处，不仅在于它引发的公众关注——它让人看到自由主义事业重新受到关注的可能——还在于它与国联的技术术语、与他们在1920年代末和1930年代初深陷其中的商业周期研究的晦涩细节相去之远。最迟到1930年代末，事情已不容争辩：全世界的统计事实加在一起，也换不来米塞斯在1920年代所辨认出的那个破碎世界的复原。
en: The most striking feature of Lippman’s book and the colloquium organized around it was that thinkers like Röpke and Hayek, who were otherwise skeptical of such forms of intervention and redistribution, would be so enthusiastic about it. One could surmise that what was most liberating about the book was not only the public attention it drew, dangling the possibility of a return to currency of the liberal cause, but also how far it was from the technical jargon of the League of Nations and the arcane details of business cycle research in which many of them had been entrenched in the late 1920s and early 1930s. By the late 1930s at the latest, it had become indisputable that all of the statistical facts in the world were not adding up to a restoration of the shattered world that Mises had identified in the 1920s.

zh: 会前，勒普克与其合著者、德国社会学家亚历山大·拉斯托把话说得最直白。他们观察到：“过去十年间，人力与物力已被动员起来，规模空前。……事实被堆叠到天上，会议接连不断地召开，经济分析被推求到愈加密致的精细——也就顺带愈益脱离现实——，庞大而细密的研究规划正被精心拟定，建制化的科学的庞大装置被架起，问卷发往几乎每一个国家、社会的每一个阶层。”而各国的联合程度却愈见其减，不见其增。
后来，勒普克不无感慨地说，正好可作本章的题辞：“说世界经济衰落的时代同时也是国际经济会议的时代，绝非夸张。”
en: Ahead of the conference Röpke and his co-author, the German sociologist Alexander Rüstow, put the matter most bluntly when they observed that “men and means have been mobilized during the last ten years, on an unprecedented scale. … Facts have been piled up sky-high, conferences have been held in endless procession, economic analysis has been brought to an ever greater degree of refinement (and incidentally to an ever greater degree of unreality), vast and detailed programs of research are being elaborated complicated machineries of institutional-ized science set up and questionnaires sent to almost every country and to every section of the population” and still nations were becoming less rather than more united.

Röpke later remarked in a rueful line that serves as the epigraph to this chapter: “It is no exaggeration to say that the era of decay of the world economy was at the same time the era of international economic conferences.”

zh: 在这种信息过剩而数据繁多却无力见效的气氛中，李普曼书中令人耳目一新之处，很可能正在于他强调的不是事实的与经济的方面，而是自由主义的政治与社会学面向。尽管他通篇处理经济议题，经济却不被写成一片数字与周期的空间，而是价值与秩序的空间。事实上，李普曼一书的一个核心论点——大体取自他对米塞斯和哈耶克的阅读——就是：企图由“明智的权威”对经济实施他所称的“自上而下的控制”，既天真又有害。
他大量借用奥地利思想家的理论，来批判他所谓社会与经济生活中的“控制幻觉”。他嘲讽这样一种企图：把人们规模庞大的协作尽收眼底、尽数理解，而这种协调主要是由只受价格自由移动支配的人们在近乎无计划的状态下完成的。他写道，任何“统计、普查、报告”的堆积，都不可能汇成足以自上而下规划这一过程的充分知识。
李普曼下面这段话可以理解为同时暗批两种企图：社会主义的计划经济，以及借商业周期研究看清整个经济生活：“面对社会经验的数据，人的心智如同一盏灯笼，在未经探索的旷野上，断续地把昏暗的光圈投向多少熟悉的一片片地面。”
他搬出了神。“社会控制，”他写道，“永远不能被视为近似于人们归之于上帝——宇宙之创造者与统治者——的那种主宰。”
en: In such an atmosphere of information glut and ineffectual data overload, what was likely refreshing in Lippmann’s book was his emphasis, not on the factual and economic, but on the political and sociological aspects of liberalism. While he engaged with economic matters throughout, the economy was cast not as a space of numbers and cycles but of values and order. In fact, one of the core arguments of Lippmann’s book, largely adopted from his reading of Mises and Hayek, was that it was naive and damaging to try to carry out what he called the “overhead control” of the economy by “intelligent authority.”

He drew on the Austrian thinkers extensively to critique what he called “the illusion of control” in social and economic life. He derided the attempt to fully capture and comprehend the vast coordination of human energies that was carried out, largely unplanned, by people driven only by the free movement of prices. No mass of “statistics, censuses, reports,” he wrote, could add up to sufficient knowledge to plan the process from above.

In what could be read as an implicit critique of both socialist planning and attempts to perceive the entirety of economic life through business cycle research, Lippmann wrote that “to the data of social experience the mind is like a lantern which casts dim circles of light spasmodically upon somewhat familiar patches of ground in an unexplored wilderness.”
He summoned the divine. “Social control,” he wrote, “can never be regarded as even an approximation to the kind of mastery which men have ascribed to God as the creator and ruler of the universe.”

zh: 面对一个“无数要素相互依赖、相互作用”的“社会系统”，该怎么办？
李普曼并未因自由主义资本主义社会天生难以治理而绝望。毋宁说，他作出了那一定义了此后组织化新自由主义的举动：他从经济转向法律。他写道：“随着事务愈发错综复杂、在时间与空间上愈见延展、愈益盘根错节、环环相扣，自上而下的指挥……不得不让位于……以普通法（common law）方法实现的社会控制。”
“发现分工的意义，是自由主义的历史使命；而其未竟的任务，则是表明法律与公共政策如何能够最好地适应这一生产方式。”
法律的作用不限于民族国家。李普曼在书中通篇使用“大社会”（the Great Society）这一范畴——借自伦敦政治经济学院经济学家格雷厄姆·沃拉斯（Graham Wallas）——用以指称一个相互联结的交换空间，其范围在现代已是全球性的。
共同的法律必须延伸及于全球的大社会。他把这一点说得斩截：“整个世界经济对共同法律的需要，乃是全人类万千众生在日常交易中须臾不可离的需要，其累积之力不可抗拒。”
en: What to do in the face of a “social system” in which “innumerable elements are interdependent and interacting”?

Lippmann did not despair at the inherent ungovernability of a liberal capitalist society. Rather, he made the move that would define much of organized neoliberalism: he moved from the economic to the legal. “As affairs become more intricate, more extended in time and space, more involved and interrelated,” he wrote, “overhead direction … has to give way … to social control by the method of a common law.”

While it was the “historic mission of liberalism to discover the significance of the division of labor; its uncompleted task is to show how law and public policy may best be adapted to this mode of production.”

The role of law was not limited to the nation-state. Throughout his book Lippmann used the category of “the Great Society,” which he borrowed from the LSE economist Graham Wallas, to connote an interconnected space of exchange whose reach by the modern age was global.

Shared law must extend throughout the global Great Society. He put the point forcefully: “The necessity of common laws throughout the world economy is the necessity of all the multitudes of mankind in all their daily transactions, and its cumulative force is invincible.”

zh: 李普曼追随米塞斯和哈耶克，提出社会主义与自由主义同样面临一个知识问题，只有自由价格体系能够解决。他又有进于米塞斯和哈耶克之处：他着重强调，价格只在统一的法律结构内才能发挥作用。本·杰克逊（Ben Jackson）指出，这一法律转向预示了哈耶克本人自1940年代起对法治的重新关注。
哈耶克和米塞斯也接纳了“大社会”一词，并在各自的学术生涯中一直使用它。林登·B.·约翰逊在1960年代末用同一个短语来命名他的整套国家福利计划，这很容易让人误判该词对于哈耶克、米塞斯、李普曼——以及先于此前的亚当·斯密——的尺度。对他们所有人来说，这个词意指市场交换领域的全幅范围；正如米塞斯1944年所言，大社会包纳“一切人”。
en: Lippmann followed Mises and Hayek by proposing that both socialism and liberalism faced a knowledge problem that only the free price system could solve. He went beyond Mises and Hayek in his strong emphasis on the fact that prices only worked within the uniform structure of law. Ben Jackson points out that this turn to law anticipated Hayek’s own renewed interest in the rule of law from the 1940s onward.

Hayek and Mises also adopted the term “The Great Society” and used it throughout their careers. The fact that Lyndon B. Johnson used the same phrase to describe his suite of national welfare state programs in the late 1960s make it easy to mistake the scale of the term for Hayek, Mises, Lippmann, and indeed Adam Smith before them. For all of them, the term meant the full reach of the realm of market exchange; the Great Society, as Mises put it in 1944, embraced “all human beings.”

zh: 李普曼的著作，是把奥地利学派关于价值主观性的观点与对法治的新关注融为一炉的产物。对哈耶克而言，它与他早在李普曼座谈会之前就已开始投入知识问题的新思路相契合。即便他们投身统计调查的种种规划，围绕米塞斯的维也纳经济学家们对纯粹描述性事实的限度以及预测的可能性始终持谨慎态度。
19世纪末，历史学派经济学与门格尔一脉的边际主义者之间的“方法论之争”（Methodenstreit），部分地就围绕着能否捕捉国民经济之总体（更遑论世界）这一怀疑展开。米塞斯圈的经济学家对恩斯特·瓦格曼在柏林的努力持怀疑态度，视之为历史学派规划的延伸。
然而直到1930年代，这个问题更多地是靠理论进路来解决的。1930年代，哈耶克重返所谓计算争论，修订了他自己对知识之作用的信念。
en: Lippmann’s work was a synthesis of the Austrian perspective on the subjectivity of value with a new attention to the rule of law. For Hayek, it dovetailed with new attention he had been devoting to the question of knowledge from even before the Lippmann Colloquium. Even as they engaged in projects of statistical inquiry, the Viennese economists around Mises had always remained cautious about the limits of purely descriptive facts and the possibility of prediction.

The Methodenstreit of the late nineteenth century between the historical economists and the marginalists associated with Carl Menger had revolved in part around the skepticism about the possibility of capturing the totality of a national economy, let alone the world. The economists of the Mises Circle were dubious about the efforts of Ernst Wagemann in Berlin as the extension of the project of the historical school.

Yet until the 1930s this problem had been solved more through theoretical approaches. In the 1930s, however, Hayek returned to the so-called calculation debate to revise his own faith in the role of knowledge itself.

zh: 1937年，在伦敦经济俱乐部发表主席演说《经济学与知识》（“Economics and Knowledge”）时，哈耶克提醒听众注意
的拉丁文本义是“被给定的”。但问题在于，他说，“事实是对谁被给定的”。
他觉得经济学家们模糊了这样一个差别：他们所知道（或自称知道）的东西，与世间普通经济行动者实际知道的东西。他在奥地利商业周期研究所的工作本以经济知识可以通过教育传递的理念为前提——市场、经济学家与经济行动者之间的鸿沟可以被弥合——可现在，他把这整个可能性都打了个问号。他指出，均衡模型既以所有参与者拥有完备知识为前提，又以他讥评为本质上行尸走肉般的经济人（
）范畴为前提——“我们曾以祈祷和斋戒驱魔赶走的‘经济人’，又从后门溜了回来。”
并非最后一次，哈耶克做了新自由主义者常被指控自己会做的那种事：他指出，经济学家把自己的模型误当成了真实世界。
en: In his presidential address, “Economics and Knowledge,” at the London Economic Club in 1937, Hayek reminded his audience of the Latin definition of
as “given.” But the issue was, he said, “to whom the facts are supposed to be given.”
He felt economists had fudged the difference between the things that they knew (or claimed to know) and the things that average economic actors in the world actu

knew. His work at the Austrian Business Cycle Research Institute had been premised on the notion of economic pedagogy—the idea that the gap between the market, the economist, and the economic actor could be bridged—but now he threw that whole possibility into doubt. He pointed out that equilibrium models were based on both perfect knowledge among all actors involved and what he derided as essenti
the zombie category of
—“the ‘economic man’ whom we have exorcised with prayer and fasting, has returned through the back door.”
Not for the last time, Hayek did something that neoliberals are often themselves accused of doing: he suggested that economists mistake their models for the real world.

zh: 在哈耶克看来，完美市场在现实中并不存在。它们不可能存在，因为完备知识是不可能的。相反，人们必须从他所称的“知识分工”的前提出发——他征引米塞斯，此说与劳动分工相类比。
他驳斥了经济学家“只需……价格知识”的想法。这是一个明确的转向：既背离晴雨表视野，也背离维也纳研究所的公众教化角色，而且干脆不再以“周期”理念作为研究焦点。1937年，哈耶克首次暗示了后来被一位学者认作其哲学标志性特征的东西：无知之用。
哈耶克提出，均衡之所以存在，“只是因为有些人没有机会得知某些事实，而这些事实倘若为他们所知，就会促使他们改变自己的计划”。
他得出的结论不仅是：完备知识是模型中不可移用于现实的一种同义反复的假设；而且它错失了根本之点：造成均衡——亦即经济秩序形态——的，是不完备的知识而非完备的知识。正如他后来所说，他在1930年代后半叶领悟到，“经济学的基本功能，是解释人类活动如何调整自身以适应人们并不知晓的事实这一过程”。
en: To Hayek, perfect markets did not exist in reality. They could not exist because perfect knowledge is impossible. Instead one had to begin from the assumption of what, quoting Mises, he called the “division of knowledge,” analogous to the division of labor.

He dismissed the economists’ idea that “only … knowledge of prices” was needed. This was a clear move away from both the barometer vision and the public pedagogy role of the Viennese research institute and away from the idea of the cycle altogether as the focus of research. It was in 1937 that Hayek first gestured at what one scholar has identified as a defining feature of his philosophy: the usefulness of ignorance.
Hayek suggested that equilibrium exists “only because some people have no chance of learning about facts which, if they knew them, would induce them to alter their plans.”

He concluded not only that perfect knowledge was a tautological conceit of the model inapplicable to reality but that it missed the basic point that imperfect, not perfect, knowledge was what created equilibrium in the form of economic order. As he put it later, he realized in the second half of the 1930s that “the basic function of economics was to explain the process of how human activity adapted itself to data

children: about which it had no information.

zh: 如果人是对市场刺激作出无意识反应的，那么顺理成章，公共启蒙便不再是经济学家的角色。商业周期曲线图确乎是“国家的脉搏”，它所记录的是自主神经系统的活动，而非有意识的思维。援引这样一条自主活动的记录，绝不是确保长期稳定的手段。事实上，假定这张图表为政策制定者提供了可付诸行动的知识，是一切错误中最具诱惑力的一种，它将导向李普曼所称的“控制幻觉”。哈耶克后来写道：甚至“谈论国民经济、社会经济或世界经济……就是这类最具社会主义色彩的企图的主要根源之一：把市场的自发秩序变成一个有意经营、为一套议定的共同目标服务的组织”。
延伸这个隐喻：哈耶克的解决办法是把病人从心电图仪上接下来，转而注重预防。目标焕然一新——不再是疾病发作时以直接行动救治，而是设计一个病人根本不会发病的世界。想象力的地平线不再是治疗，而是预防。
en: If humans acted in unconscious response to market stimuli, then it followed that public enlightenment was no longer the role of the economist. The business cycle chart was truly the pulse of the nation in the sense of being a record of the autonomous nervous system rather than the thinking mind. Reference to such a record of autonomous activity would be no means of ensuring greater stability over time. In fact, to assume that the chart provided actionable knowledge for the policy maker was the most seductive error of all, leading to what Lippmann called the “illusion of control.” As Hayek wrote later, to even “speak of a national social or world economy … is one of the chief sources of the most socialist endeavor to turn the spontaneous order of the market into a deliberately run organization serving an agreed system of common ends.”

To extend the metaphor, Hayek’s solution was to remove the patient from the electrocardiograph and focus on preventative care. There was a new goal—not to cure maladies as they arose through direct action but to design a world where the patient would never fall sick in the first place. The horizon of imagination was not treatment but prophylaxis.

zh: 李普曼书中对制度与法治的强调，为哈耶克关于知识有限的结论提供了绝佳的补充，使人们得以从以数字或理论模型捕捉经济的种种尝试，转向法律与治国之术的规划。李普曼在召唤自由主义者作为秩序设计者的新角色时，颂扬了选择性知识的重要性：“思想家坐在书斋里勾画社会运转的蓝图，倘若他的早餐不是由一个超出其细致理解力的社会过程为他置办好的，他就根本无从思考。他知道，他的早餐有赖于巴西咖啡种植园的工人、佛罗里达柑橘园里的果农、古巴的蔗农、达科他州的小麦农、纽约的奶牛场；早餐经轮船、铁路和卡车汇集而来，以宾夕法尼亚的煤为燃料，用铝、瓷、钢和玻璃制成的器具烹调。可是，一顿早餐的复杂程度，假如使它得以摆上桌的每一个过程都必须刻意规划，就将超出任何心智的理解力。”与那些把现象学意义上的相遇时刻当作理解世界经济之入口的经济学家——后来的著名例子是米尔顿·弗里德曼和他的铅笔——不同，李普曼把它当作忘掉世界经济的时刻。他写道：“正是因为可以依靠一套极为复杂的日常协作，人才能吃上早餐，然后思考新的社会秩序。”
自由主义知识人的任务，不是描摹世界经济的轮廓，而是退后一步，沉思那个更大秩序本身的赖以成立的根本条件。全球经济是不可知的——而这并非死胡同，而是设计秩序的起点：世界经济得以在其中繁荣的秩序。这一洞见是日内瓦学派的新自由主义得以兴起的基石。
en: The emphasis on institutions and rule of law in Lippmann’s book offered a perfect complement to Hayek’s conclusion about limited knowledge, allowing for a turn away from attempts to capture the economy in either numbers or theoretical models and toward projects of law and statecraft. Lippmann praised the importance of selective knowledge when he conjured up a new role for the liberal as architect of order: “The thinker, as he sits in his study drawing his plans for the direction of society, will do no thinking if his breakfast has not been produced for him by a social process which is beyond his detailed comprehension. He knows that his breakfast depends upon workers on the coffee plantations of Brazil, the citrus groves of Florida, the sugar fields of Cuba, the wheat farms of the Dakotas, the dairies of New York; that it has been assembled by ships, railroads, and trucks, has been cooked with coal from Pennsylvania in utensils made of aluminum, china, steel, and glass. But the intricacy of one breakfast, if every process that brought it to the table had deliberately to be planned, would be beyond the understanding of any mind.” Unlike those economists—including the later famous case of Milton Friedman and his pencil—who took the moment of phenomenological encounter as an entry point into understanding the world economy, Lippmann suggested it as a moment to forget the world economy. “Only because he can count upon an infinitely complex system of working routines,” he wrote, “can a man eat his breakfast and then think about a new social order.”

The task of the liberal intellectual was not to seek to trace the lineaments of the world economy but to take a step back and contemplate the core enabling conditions of the grander order itself. The global economy was unknowable—and this was not a dead end but the starting point for designing the order within which the world economy could thrive. This insight was foundational to the emergence of the Geneva School of neoliberalism.

zh: 1930年代离开数字的第二条路，由勒普克和拉斯托走过。座谈会上，勒普克提出了两年前他在一封致罗宾斯信中已经抛出的一种理论：“我们这套体制之道德功能的瓦解，是当下瓦解进程中最重要的、也最不祥的方面。”
他写道，自由主义需要“向保守主义学习”的，是关注“那些难以称量之物、生命的或人的要素，或者不管你怎样称呼这些难以捉摸的东西”。
与李普曼一样，勒普克和拉斯托认为，对自由放任的误信产生了不良的社会后果，最集中的表达便是那种叫作“无产阶级”的“疾病”。“狭隘的”人性经济观忽视了人之为人的“超经济”需要。
en: The second road away from numbers in the 1930s was taken by Röpke and Rüstow. At the colloquium, Röpke advanced a theory he had floated in a letter to Robbins two years earlier that “the disintegration of the moral function of our system is the most important and the most sinister aspect of the process of the present disintegration.”
He wrote that what liberalism had to “learn from conservatism” was to pay attention to “the imponderabilia, the vital or human element or whatever you call these elusive things.”

Like Lippmann, Röpke and Rüstow held that the misguided belief in laissez-faire had produced adverse social effects, best expressed in the “disease called ‘proletariat.’ ” A “narrow economic conception” of humanity had overlooked the “extra-economic” needs of humanity.

zh: 拉斯托在李普曼座谈会上说：“市场已沦为原子化的领域”，而相信市场“自行运转”则是一种“神学—理性主义的错误”——此言预演了卡尔·波兰尼在《大转型》（The Great Transformation）中对市场原教旨主义的分析。
对效率、利润与生产率的片面专注，造成了有害于社会生活的孤立与道德的退化，因为个人脱离了共同体的一切纽带。在一个残酷的悖论中，被剪断一切社会纽带、在世界中随波逐流的这种处境，“从市场经济的观点看，反倒像是摆脱了摩擦与超经济的拖累”。
拉斯托和勒普克虽未使用“嵌入”（embeddedness）一词本身，却实际上主张经济必须重新嵌入社会。个人必须重新找到有意义的共同体关系，包括家庭、宗教，并且最好是与乡土的联系。
en: Prefiguring Karl Polanyi’s analysis of market fundamentalism in
Rüstow said at the Lippmann Colloquium that “the market had become a domain of atomization” and the belief that the market “operates by itself” was a “theologico-rational error.”

One-sided focus on efficiency, profit, and productivity had led to a sociologically damaging isolation and the degeneration of morality as the individual became detached from all community. In a cruel paradox, the experience of being severed from all social ties and set adrift in the world “appears from the point of view of the market economy as liberation from friction and extra-economic drag.”

Without using the term “embeddedness” itself, Rüstow and Röpke effectively argued that the economy must be re-embedded in society. The individual must rediscover meaningful community relationships, including family, religion and, preferably, a connection to the rural land.

zh: 哈耶克和米塞斯在座谈会上公开反对勒普克和拉斯托。米塞斯指责拉斯托美化乡村生活；哈耶克则提出，为“生命价值”制定“等级量表”的建议与自由主义原则相抵触。
这一分歧日后将在种族问题上重新浮现，第5章将会看到。然而把众人联结在一起的，第一是他们对国际主义的信念，第二是他们对数字与模型能否道出世界真相的怀疑。勒普克斥责社会科学沦落为“一架记录事实的机器”，并呼吁更多综合性的协作研究——不像商业周期研究所那种统计数字的收集，而更像国际研究会议对国际关系的考察和李普曼的社会哲学。
en: Hayek and Mises opposed Röpke and Rüstow openly at the colloquium. Mises accused Rüstow of romanticizing rural life, and Hayek argued that the proposal for a “rating scale” of “vital values” was inconsistent with the principles of liberalism.

This divergence would resurface again on the question of race, as Chapter 5 will show. What they all united on, however, was, first, their belief in internationalism, and, second, their skepticism about the value of numbers and models in telling the truth about the world. Röpke disparaged the declension of the social sciences into “a fact-recording machinery” and called for more synthetic collaborative work—less like the statistics-gathering of the business cycle research institutes and more like the international relations investigations of the ISC and the social philosophy of Lippmann.

zh: 对统计学最激烈的攻击，也许来自波兰经济学家、拉帕德研究院的教职成员迈克尔·海尔佩林。他在李普曼座谈会后返回日内瓦后的次月完成了他的一本书，后来又把它压缩改写，作为对ISC 1939年会议的贡献。在全书开头几页，海尔佩林警告“伪数量概念”之弊，批评用“统计建构”去理解“它们本应代表的那个驳杂多样的现实”。他抱怨道：“我们对于经济现实的知识，正在变成一种指数知识。”
统计学提供了一条“摆脱经济世界令人困惑的多样与杂多”的舒适出路，“可是这种多样性确确实实地存在，无视它，人就会对世界和经济过程作出错误或无意义的陈述”。
曾被视为世界经济洞见之王道大路的统计规划，已经走进了死胡同。
en: Perhaps the most strident attack on statistics came from the Polish economist and faculty member at Rappard’s Graduate Institute, Michael Heilperin, in a book he completed the month after returning to Geneva from the Lippmann Colloquium and later condensed for his contribution to the ISC in 1939. In the book’s first pages, Heilperin warned of “pseudo-quantitative concepts” and criticized the use of “statistical constructions” to understand “the heterogeneous reality they are supposed to represent.” He complained that “our knowledge of economic reality tends to become an index-number knowledge.”

Statistics offered “a comfortable way out of the perplexing multiplicity and heterogeneity presented by the economic world … but the multiplicity does exist and by ignoring it one falls into erroneous or meaningless statements about the world and about economic processes.”
Once deemed the royal road to world economic insight, projects of statistics had led into a dead end.

zh: 核心新自由主义者在1930年代初在研究实践中相信数字可以发挥作用，到十年结束时却转为对数字的厌恶。即便是原本就对描述性统计心存怀疑的奥地利人，也曾乐意推广带有公众教化功能的商业周期研究。而到十年之末，哈耶克已在谈论“不知”对于经济关系的必要性。如何解释这一集体转向？从对“控制幻觉”的谴责中不难窥见端倪：在整个1930年代，数字的使用已经同那些主张由国家行动稳定价格水平的人，以及同奥托·诺伊拉特、哈罗德·拉斯基这类左派联结在一起——李普曼指控后者图谋通过“经济世界规划”建立一个“行星尺度的超级国家”。
对于一个刚刚自我指认的新自由主义群体来说，一个奠基性的区分就在于：他们不像左派对手那样相信经济可以被看见、被计算——因而可以被微调、被完善。面对他们所认定的价格机制之瘫损与“退化”，新自由主义者把重注押在经济的不可见性上。无法看清的经济，也无法靠人为设计加以塑造。
en: The core neoliberals began the 1930s with a working faith in numbers but ended the decade with an antipathy toward them. Even the Austrians with their preexisting skepticism toward descriptive statistics had been willing to promote business cycle research with a public pedagogical function. Yet by the end of the decade, Hayek was speaking of the necessity of not-knowing for economic relations. What explains the collective shift? As suggested in the condemnation of the “illusion of control,” over the 1930s the use of numbers had become associated with those who believed in state action to stabilize the price level and leftists like Otto Neurath and Harold Laski, whom Lippmann accused of seeking a “planetary super-state” through “economic world-planning.”

It was a founding distinction for the newly self-identifying group of neoliberals that they did not share the belief of their opponents on the left that the economy could be seen and counted—and, thus, fine-tuned and perfected. In response to what they saw as the crippling and “degeneration” of the functioning price system, neoliberals invested heavily in the invisibility of the economy. What could not be seen could not be engineered.

zh: 如果经济超出表征之外，那么任务便是寻找一个框架来容纳并保护它。1938年的李普曼座谈会产出了一幅世界的规范性图景：其中最切要的干预手段不在度量、观察或监视，而在确立一套共同的可执行的法律，并确立一种方式来安顿市场所提供不了的、人的基本需要。把经济置于表征空间之外——对哈耶克而言甚至置于理性之外——新自由主义遂在1930年代末作为一种综合社会科学的规划诞生；说来令人惊讶，在这一规划里，最不重要的学科进路恰恰是经济学本身。
en: If the economy was beyond representation, then the task was to find a framework to contain and protect it. The Lippmann Colloquium in 1938 yielded a normative vision of the world in which the most relevant means of intervention was not in measurement, observation, or surveillance but in the establishment of a common, enforceable law and a means of accounting for the vital needs of humanity not provided by the market. By placing the economy beyond the space of representation—and, for Hayek, beyond even reason—neoliberalism was born in the late 1930s as a project of synthetic social science in which, as surprising as it might sound, the least important disciplinary approach was that of economics itself.

zh: 日内瓦学派新自由主义的规划虽诞生于全球统计与数据汇集的种种规划，其主旨却不是观看世界经济，而是宣布它的不可见；不是度量它，而是把它塑造为崇高不可捕捉之物；不是勘察它的运行，而是把它理论化为一个难以理解的自发秩序（spontaneous order）。日内瓦学派的新自由主义将是否定神学。它的纲领是设计恰当的制度，把世界经济围封起来，而不描述世界经济本身。这将是一个法律、国家与组织在全球层面的规划。耐人寻味的是，米塞斯在李普曼座谈会上的最后一次发言，是提议研究国际联盟。

他绝不是一个相信有神奇自我组织市场的“古自由主义者”（paleoliberal）；他和所有新自由主义者一样，把这个智识规划看作寻找服务于市场秩序的恰当国家与恰当法律。1933年，H. G. 威尔斯出版了一部小说《未来的形状》（The Shape of Things to Come），假托是国联雇用的经济学家菲利普·雷文博士的梦记；此人于1930年11月“意外身亡”。雷文一直在梦见未来，他的日记把国联的愿景向前投射。书中谈到设一个中央观测局——“一套由讨论、计算、批评与预测构成的复杂机构”——和一个“世界百科全书机构”，坐落于“母思想城”——明摆着的日内瓦替身。那是未来的一个版本：科学知识完备无遗，未来之事洞若观火。经济学家们忙于记录“反常并制定调整方案”。雷文记述道，这一愿景的突破口先是大战，此后“世界秩序”的观念成为许多人的“切实可用的信念”，而真正深入人心则是在“1928年与1929年的金融风暴”之后——它们使“世界国家的先知们”平添了持守其信念的勇气——“他们已经认识到，人类社会变成了一个不可分割的经济体系”。
en: Although born out of projects of global statistics and data gathering, the project of Geneva School neoliberalism would be not about seeing the world economy but about declaring its invisibility; not measuring it but casting it as sublime and beyond capture; not surveying its work-ings but theorizing it as a spontaneous order eluding comprehension. Geneva School neoliberalism would be a negative theology. Its program was to design the right institutions to encase the world economy without describing the world economy itself. This would be a project of law, state and organizations at the global level. It is telling that Mises’s last intervention at the Lippmann Colloquium was to suggest the study of the League of Nations.

Far from being a paleoliberal who believed in a magical, self-organizing market, he, like all neoliberals, saw the intellectual project as finding the right state and the right law to serve the market order. In 1933 H. G. Wells published a novel,

children: The Shape of Things to Come,

en: that purported to be the dream journal of Dr. Philip Raven, an economist in the employ of the League of Nations who met an “unexpected death” in November 1930. Raven had been dreaming of the future, and his journal projected the vision of the League forward. It spoke of a Central Observation Bureau—a “complex organization of discussion, calculation, criticism and forecast” and a “World Encyclopaedia Establishment” in the “mother thought-city”—a transparent stand-in for Geneva. It was a version of the future where scientific knowledge was complete and coming events were an open book. Economists kept busy recording “irregularities and producing plans for adjustment.” Raven recorded that the breakthrough for this vision had been first the Great War, after which the idea of “worldwide order” became a “working conviction” for many but really took hold after the “financial storms of the years 1928 and 1929,” which gave “the World-State prophets the courage of their conviction”—“they had arrived at the realization that human society had become one indivisible economic system.”

zh: 大萧条的全球螺旋已确凿无疑地证明，存在一个叫作世界经济的相互依赖的实体。1931年7月，米塞斯出席的一次国际商会会议将这种观感一语道破：“世界危机的发展已清楚表明各国之间经济与金融的相互依赖。”

新自由主义者得出了与威尔斯笔下的虚构经济学家以及国际商会相同的结论。但他们的路径并不通往中央观测局或世界百科全书。他们并没有以全景之梦结束这个十年。的确，他们把雷文——以及威尔斯——的幻想看作恰恰暴露了大萧条之后那场灾难的病根。从罗斯福的新政到希特勒的新秩序再到斯大林的五年计划，新自由主义者看到各国政府耽于控制的幻觉，误信运用科学知识，能让位居顶层的“明智的权威”看清国民经济的全貌，从而使这样的计划成为可能：国民经济在孤立与自主中长存。
en: The global spiral of the Great Depression had proven beyond a doubt that there was an interdependent entity called the world economy. A meeting of the ICC attended by Mises summarized the sentiment in July 1931 when they declared, “The development of the world crisis has clearly demonstrated the economic and financial interdependence of all nations.”

The neoliberals had come to the same conclusion as Wells’s fictional economist and the ICC. Yet their path did not lead to the Central Observation Bureau or the World Encyclopedia. They did not end the decade dreaming of synopsis. Indeed, they saw the fantasies of Raven—and Wells—as revealing the very root of the catastrophe that followed the Depression. From Roosevelt’s New Deal to Hitler’s New Order to Stalin’s Five-Year Plan, neoliberals saw governments indulging in illusions of control and the misguided belief that applied scientific knowledge could make national economies transparent to an “intelligent authority” from above, enabling plans by which national economies could persist in isolation and autonomy.

zh: 1930年代末，越来越多的论者提出：只要能正确地看见经济，那么正如雷文所写，“调整方案”就能阻止未来的萧条。如今已获广泛承认，“经济”本身作为可以观察、建立模型并加以设计和改造的对象这一观念，只是随着国民收入核算工具的成熟和宏观经济学学科的建立才兴起的。
勒普克本人1937年就指出，宏观经济学助长了国家取向的政策框架，包括他所谓“自我封闭的国民收入理论”。
规划项目把民族国家当作默认的实施范围，有时还明言如此，后来的福利国家也在这一范围内提供社会服务和给付。日内瓦学派的新自由主义者认为这种自信错置了对象，在本应以世界为分析框架之处画地为牢。哈耶克1937年在拉帕德的日内瓦研究院的一次演讲中说，稳定价格水平的想法“在很大程度上建立在一种幻觉之上，而该幻觉又起因于这样一个偶然事实：衡量价格变动的统计指标通常恰好是按国家本身编制的”。
米塞斯在日内瓦完成的一部书中写道，统计学是记录历史的方式，而非生产理论的方式，“与经济学毫无干系”。
数字与周期的世界制造了一种全幅洞见的假象，掩盖了干预的副作用。勒普克同年在这所研究院的就职演讲中指出，“世界确实已开始相信，经济体制只要引导得当，便可制成免于周期的体制”，但他追问：“倘若那些免于周期的经济原来不过是一场视觉幻觉——不可避免的经济失调并非在其发生之地显现，而是被推到经济体系的外围——那又将如何？”
en: In the late 1930s ever more thinkers suggested that if you could only see the economy correctly, then just as Raven wrote, “plans for adjustments” could prevent future depressions. As is now widely acknowledged, the idea of “the economy” itself as an object to be observed, modeled, and engineered only arose with the tools of national income accounting and the creation of the discipline of macroeconomics.
Röpke himself pointed out in 1937 that macroeconomics encouraged the national frame of policy, including what he called “self-contained national income theory.”

The nation-state was the assumed, if not the explicit, container for projects of planning and later the distribution of the welfare state’s social services and benefits. Geneva School neoliberals felt that this confidence was misplaced and drew a line around the nation when the frame of analysis should encompass the world. In a lecture at Rappard’s Institute in Geneva in 1937, Hayek said that the idea of stabilizing the price level “rests largely on an illusion, based on the accident that the statistical measure of price movements are usually constructed for countries as such.”
In a book he finished in Geneva, Mises wrote that statistics were a way of recording history, not producing theory, and had “nothing to do with economics.”

The world of numbers and cycles gave a false impression of total vision that hid the side effects of intervention. In his inaugural lecture at the Institute in the same year, Röpke suggested that “the world has indeed come to believe that the economic system, if properly guided, can be made cycle-proof” but wondered if “those cycle-proof economies turn out to be an optical illusion, as where the unavoidable economic disharmonies will not become manifest at the place of their origin, but rather be shoved off to the periphery of the economic apparatus.”

zh: 新自由主义者以研究商业周期开启1930年代。到十年之末，商业周期可以被驯服、被控制的观念日益流行，反而使他们把这种信念视为“国际经济解体”的主要成因之一。
勒普克在李普曼座谈会上说：“最大的危险是新的商业周期政策：经济自主的政策、经济民族主义的政策，与计划经济和闭关自足的统制相结合。”
通过统计和周期来认识经济，养成了在国家尺度上驾驭经济的幻想，大有为全球的无序铺平道路之势。
en: Neoliberals began the 1930s studying the business cycle. By the end of the decade, the spreading belief that the business cycle could be tamed and controlled led them to see it as one of the chief causes of “international economic disintegration.”

Röpke said at the Lippmann Colloquium: “The greatest danger is the new business cycle policy: the policy of economic autonomy, the policy of economic nationalism, combined with the planned economy and autarchy.”
Seeing economics through statistics and cycles had fostered fantasies of management at the scale of the nation that threatened to pave the way to global disorder.

zh: 1930年代改变了自由主义关于世界经济的思考。1920年代的前提是：复原破碎的全球经济是一个消极过程。只要工会筑起的工资要求之墙和特殊利益集团筑起的关税之墙垮塌，自由市场便会接管。世界经济在一代人之内遭遇第二次灾难性崩溃，使许多知识分子重新思考这个问题。新自由主义（
liberalism）规划的实质在于：保卫世界经济不能只是一个消极的规划，而必须是一个主动建构的规划。法律与国家有了新的角色。新自由主义者在1930年代开辟的，是以秩序思考的理念——把自由主义与社会主义之争，看作一个需要全系统视野的问题。
en: The 1930s transformed liberal thinking about the world economy. The premise of the 1920s had been that restoring the shattered global economy was a negative process. If the walls of wage demands created by unions and of tariffs created by special interests would fall, then the free market would take over. The second catastrophic collapse of the world economy in a single generation made many intellectuals think about the problem anew. The essence of the project of
liberalism was that defending the world economy could not be a simply negative project but had to be a proactive project. There was a new role for law and the state. What
liberals pioneered in the 1930s was the idea of thinking in orders, seeing the question of liberalism versus socialism as one that required a total-system perspective.

zh: 在凯恩斯、莫斯科和沙赫特启发的种种解决方案多为国家本位、计划之风弥漫的十年里，勒普克和他的合作者在巴黎、日内瓦和东欧以全球的尺度思考。他们的讨论发端于与国际关系学科同一个母体。尽管今天全球主义（globalism）几乎成了美国权力的同义词，1930年代却全然不同。全球主义并非一种径直由美国向外辐射的意识形态。把世界作为对象的多数规划，设在巴黎、日内瓦和伦敦，而不是华盛顿或纽约。国际关系史往往略去它在战间期的欧洲起源——它被战后的范式遮蔽了。但新自由主义本属国际关系发轫时提出的问题之列。后续各章将追踪新自由主义者曾经参与的一系列制度设计——它们常常失败——以保卫全球经济。第3章将展示其中一些最明确的例子：新自由主义的联邦制方案提出的，是一套统治资本主义双重世界的双重政府。
en: In a decade when most solutions inspired by Keynes, Moscow, and Schacht were national, and planning was in the air, Röpke and his collaborators in Paris, Geneva, and Eastern Europe thought at the scale of the globe. Their discussions came out of the same milieu as the discipline of international relations. Although globalism is now nearly synonymous with American power, the 1930s were quite different. Globalism was not an ideology that simply emanated outward from the United States. Most projects that took the world as their object were based in Paris, Geneva, and London rather than Washington or New York. Histories of international relations tend to elide its European origins in the interwar period, eclipsed as it was by the postwar paradigm. But neoliberalism was part of the questions asked at the dawn of international relations. The following chapters track the series of institutional projects, often failed, that neoliberals participated in to secure the global economy. Chapter 3 shows some of the most explicit examples as neoliberal plans for federation proposed a double government to rule over capitalism’s doubled world.
